reference_drawer.description: Essential exposed-surface formulas for combinations of solids.

items.rule: Curved surface area of a cone.

items.example: Exclude circular faces when hidden or not covered.

concepts.title: 1. Exposed Surface Areas
concepts.subtitle: Count outer surfaces only
concepts.summary: For combined solids, include only surfaces visible from outside. Internal touching faces are not exposed.

points.text: Identify every exposed curved or flat surface.
Exclude internal interfaces such as the shared circle where solids join.

concepts.title: 3. Cylinder, Dome and Capsule
concepts.subtitle: Shared circular faces are hidden
concepts.summary: A cylinder with a cone or dome on top exposes the cylinder wall plus the upper curved surface. A capsule exposes the cylinder wall and two hemispherical ends.

points.text: Use $2\pi rh$ for the cylindrical curved surface.
Use $\pi rl$ for a cone or $2\pi r^2$ for a hemisphere.

concepts.subtitle: Curved cylinder wall plus conical roof

steps.strategy_question: Which move correctly separates the cone height from the total height?
strategy_options: Subtract the hemisphere radius to get $h_{cone}=15.5-3.5=12.0\text{ cm}$.
Add the radius to get $h_{cone}=15.5+3.5=19.0\text{ cm}$.
Take half the total height to get $h_{cone}=7.75\text{ cm}$.
Use the total height as the cone height $h_{cone}=15.5\text{ cm}$.

schema_notes.atomic_progression: Each question follows the specified sequence: identify dimensions → calculate slant height if needed → identify exposed surfaces and omit internal touching faces → calculate component surface areas → sum to the combination surface area.
schema_notes.strict_options_rule: Every strategy option and option_details text combines an instruction with actual mathematical content; all mathematical expressions are wrapped in single dollar signs.
schema_notes.svg_rule: Every pool question contains a mandatory responsive SVG using viewBox 0 0 280 180 and a diagram appropriate to the combined solid.
schema_notes.latex_compliance: All equations, worked examples and rubric mathematics use multiline aligned LaTeX with at most one equals sign per line.
schema_notes.guided_calculation_compliance: Every step has exactly two vertically stacked outputs and every field uses placeholder Enter value. Prompts and labels do not reveal answers.
schema_notes.pool_compliance: Each of the five typologies contains exactly 12 unique questions: 4 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
